questions.question: Directive Principles of State Policy are borrowed from:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ireland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)** are contained in **Part IV** of the **Constitution of India**, covering **Articles 36 to 51**.
 
• The concept was borrowed from the **Irish Constitution of 1937**, which had itself borrowed it from the **Spanish Constitution**.
 
• These principles serve as guidelines or **instruments of instruction** for the government to establish a **socialist, secular, and democratic** state as envisioned in the **Preamble**.
 
• Unlike **Fundamental Rights**, the DPSPs are **non-justiciable**, meaning they cannot be enforced by a court of law; however, they are **fundamental in the governance** of the country.
 
• The primary objective of these principles is to ensure **social and economic justice** and to transform India into a **Welfare State**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other major sources of the Indian Constitution include:
 
 
• **United States of America**: Source for **Fundamental Rights**, **Judicial Review**, **Preamble**, and the **Impeachment of the President**.
 
• **United Kingdom**: Contributed the **Parliamentary form of government**, **Rule of Law**, **Single Citizenship**, and the **Cabinet System**.
 
• **Canada**: Provided the framework for a **Federation with a strong Centre**, **Residuary Powers** with the Centre, and the **Advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court**.
 
• **Australia**: Inspired the **Concurrent List** and the **Joint Sitting** of the two houses of Parliament.
 
• **Soviet Union (USSR)**: The concept of **Fundamental Duties** and the ideals of **justice (social, economic, and political)** in the Preamble.

questions.question: Which of the following states has a bicameral legislature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the Indian political system, a **bicameral legislature** refers to a state government that consists of two distinct houses: the **Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha)** and the **Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad)**.
 
• **Article 168** of the **Indian Constitution** provides for the constitution of legislatures in states. While most states have a **unicameral** system, **Bihar** is one of the few that maintains both houses.
 
• The **Bihar Legislative Council** is a permanent body and was first established in **1912**. It represents the upper house of the state legislature, ensuring a system of checks and balances over the popularly elected **Legislative Assembly**.
 
• Currently, only six states in India have a bicameral arrangement: **Andhra Pradesh**, **Telangana**, **Uttar Pradesh**, **Bihar**, **Maharashtra**, and **Karnataka**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Unicameral States**:

 
 
• States like **Haryana**, **Rajasthan**, and **Himachal Pradesh** possess a **unicameral legislature**, meaning they only have the **Legislative Assembly**.
 
• In these states, the legislative process is streamlined into a single house, and all legislative powers are vested in the **Vidhan Sabha**.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Provisions for Legislative Councils**:
 
 
• Under **Article 169**, the **Parliament of India** has the authority to create or abolish a **Legislative Council** in a state if the **Legislative Assembly** of that state passes a resolution by a **special majority**.
 
• The total number of members in the **Legislative Council** of a state cannot exceed **one-third** of the total membership of the **Legislative Assembly** and must not be less than **40**.
 
• Members of the **Legislative Council (MLCs)** are chosen through various methods, including election by local bodies, graduates, teachers, and nomination by the **Governor**.

questions.question: In the Indian Census, the working population is classified into which of the following three categories?

options.text: Main workers, marginal workers, and non-workers

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Main workers, marginal workers, and non-workers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Census of India** classifies the entire population into three categories based on economic activity: **Main Workers**, **Marginal Workers**, and **Non-workers**.
 
• **Main Workers** are individuals who worked for a major part of the reference year, specifically for at least **183 days** (six months) or more. This group constitutes the primary workforce contributing to the **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**.
 
• **Marginal Workers** are those who worked for less than **183 days** in the reference year. This category often includes seasonal laborers in the **Agricultural sector** or temporary workers in the informal economy.
 
• **Non-workers** are persons who did not participate in any economically productive activity during the entire reference period. This includes **students**, **rentiers**, **dependents**, **pensioners**, and individuals engaged in **unpaid household duties**.
 
• According to the **2011 Census**, the work participation rate in India was approximately **39.8 percent**, meaning nearly **60 percent** of the population were classified as non-workers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Conceptual Distinctions**:

 
 
• **Agricultural, Industrial, and Service Workers**: These terms describe the **Three-Sector Model** of an economy rather than the specific demographic classification used by the **Registrar General of India**.
 
• **Organized and Unorganized**: These refer to the **regulatory framework** of employment. The **unorganized sector** comprises units typically not registered with the government and where labor laws are not strictly enforced.
 
• **Migrant Workers**: This classification is based on the **place of birth** or **place of last residence** being different from the place of enumeration, rather than employment duration.
 
 
 
• **Census Sub-categories**:
 
 
• The **Census** further divides workers into four broad occupational categories: **Cultivators**, **Agricultural Labourers**, **Household Industry Workers**, and **Other Workers** (including trade, commerce, and construction).
 
• Data from the **2011 Census** highlighted that **Agricultural Labourers** and **Cultivators** still make up the largest portion of the Indian workforce, despite the growing **Service Sector**.

questions.question: Which act created a separate authority for food safety in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006** was enacted to consolidate various existing laws related to food safety and standards into a single, comprehensive framework in India.
 
• This Act mandated the establishment of the **Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)**, which serves as the apex statutory body for regulating food products and ensuring their safety for human consumption.
 
• The legislation aimed to replace a multi-level, multi-departmental control system with a single integrated line of command, shifting from a **regulatory** to a **self-compliance** based approach.
 
• It repealed several older and overlapping laws, including the **Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954**, the **Fruit Products Order, 1955**, the **Meat Food Products Order, 1973**, and the **Edible Oils Packaging (Regulation) Order, 1998**.
 
• The **FSSAI** operates under the administrative jurisdiction of the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare** and is responsible for framing science-based standards and guidelines for food items.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Food Security Act, 2013**:

 
 
• The primary objective is to provide **nutritional security** by ensuring access to adequate quantities of quality food at subsidized prices to approximately **two-thirds** of India's population.
 
• It grants legal entitlements to existing programs like the **Public Distribution System (PDS)** and the **Mid-Day Meal Scheme**.
 
 
 
• **Competition Act, 2002**:
 
 
• This Act replaced the **MRTP Act, 1969** and established the **Competition Commission of India (CCI)** to prevent practices that have an adverse effect on market competition.
 
• It regulates mergers, acquisitions, and **anti-competitive agreements** to ensure fair trade and consumer welfare.
 
 
 
• **Consumer Protection Act, 2019**:
 
 
• It replaced the 1986 legislation to address modern challenges such as **e-commerce** and misleading advertisements.
 
• It established the **Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA)** to protect, promote, and enforce the rights of consumers as a class.

questions.question:
Which of the following pair is correct regarding several categories of land mentioned in Chola inscriptions?

I. Shalabhoga - land for the maintenance of a school. II. Devadana, tirunamattukkani - land gifted to temples.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Chola inscriptions** (9th to 13th centuries) provide a meticulous record of land administration, classifying land into several distinct categories based on the recipient and the purpose of the grant.
 
• **Shalabhoga** was the specific nomenclature used for land designated for the **maintenance of a school**. The term is derived from **Shala** (educational institution) and **Bhoga** (possession or enjoyment), indicating that the revenue from such lands was exclusively utilized for educational purposes and supporting scholars. **Hence, statement I is correct.**
 
• **Devadana** and **Tirunamattukkani** refer to lands **gifted to temples**. These grants were vital for the **socio-economic** role of temples in the Chola period, allowing them to function as centers of religious, cultural, and economic activity. Such lands were often exempt from tax or had their revenues redirected to the temple treasury. **Hence, statement II is correct.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Chola land revenue system also recognized other significant categories:
 
 
• **Vellanvagai**: This was land held by **non-Brahmana peasant proprietors**. It represented the most common form of landholding and was the primary source of **state revenue**.
 
• **Brahmadeya**: These were lands donated to **Brahmanas**. These grants led to the emergence of prosperous Brahmana settlements, particularly in the fertile **Kaveri valley**, where local assemblies known as **Sabhas** managed the land.
 
• **Pallichchhandam**: This category referred to land donated to **Jaina institutions**, reflecting the pluralistic religious patronage of the Chola monarchs.
 
• **Land Grants**: These grants were typically recorded on **copper plates** or engraved on the stone walls of temples to ensure permanence and legal validity, detailing the boundaries and the rights of the donees.

questions.question: In November 2024, who launched the "Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat" campaign aiming to make India child marriage-free?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Annapurna Devi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **November 2024**, the **Union Minister for Women and Child Development**, **Annapurna Devi**, officially launched the **Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat** (Child Marriage Free India) campaign to eliminate the social evil of child marriage.
 
• The campaign is designed to be a **Jan Andolan** (people’s movement), encouraging community participation to ensure every child is protected from early marriage and provided with opportunities for **education** and growth.
 
• The initiative emphasizes the effective implementation of the **Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006**, and seeks to empower local governance bodies like **Panchayats** to monitor and prevent such instances.
 
• This movement is part of the government's broader vision of **Viksit Bharat**, recognizing that ending child marriage is crucial for improving **Maternal and Child Health** and overall human development indices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Annapurna Devi**:

 
 
• She is a senior political leader serving as the **Union Minister of Women and Child Development** since **June 2024**.
 
• Before her current role, she served as the **Union Minister of State for Education**, where she focused on foundational literacy and the **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020**.
 
 
 
• **Child Marriage Regulations in India**:
 
 
• The legal age for marriage in India is currently **18 years** for females and **21 years** for males.
 
• Violations under the **Prohibition of Child Marriage Act** can lead to rigorous imprisonment of up to **two years** and a fine of up to **1 lakh rupees**.
 
• The government also utilizes the **Childline 1098** service as a critical tool for reporting and intervening in cases of potential child marriages.

questions.question: How many members of Parliament are required to initiate impeachment of the President of India?

options.text: 100 from the house of the people
One-fourth of the total membership of either House

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**One-fourth of the total membership of either House**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **President of India** can be removed from office by a process of **impeachment** for the **'violation of the Constitution'** as per **Article 61**.
 
• The process can be initiated by **either House of Parliament** (**Lok Sabha** or **Rajya Sabha**) by framing specific charges.
 
• To **initiate** the impeachment proceedings, the charges must be contained in a resolution that has been signed by at least **one-fourth of the total membership** of the House in which the charge is originated.
 
• A **14 days' notice** in writing, signed by the required number of members, must be given to the **President** before the resolution can be moved.
 
• After the resolution is moved, it must be passed by a **special majority** of **two-thirds of the total membership** of that House.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Investigation by the Second House**:

 
 
• Once the first House passes the resolution, the **other House** investigates the charges or causes them to be investigated.
 
• The **President** has the right to appear and to be represented at such an investigation to defend themselves.
 
 
 
• **Final Resolution**:
 
 
• If the investigating House also sustains the charges and passes the impeachment resolution by a majority of **two-thirds of the total membership**, the President stands removed from office.
 
• The removal is effective from the **date** on which the resolution is so passed by the second House.
 
 
 
• **Participation Details**:
 
 
• The **nominated members** of either House of Parliament can participate in the **impeachment**, although they do not vote in the Presidential election.
 
• The elected members of the **Legislative Assemblies** of States and Union Territories do not participate in the impeachment process.
 
 
 
• **Article 56**: Provides that the President shall hold office for a term of **five years** but can be removed via the procedure laid down in **Article 61**.

questions.question: Which brain structure is responsible for releasing growth hormone-releasing factor in humans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hypothalamus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Hypothalamus** is a small but critical region of the **forebrain** located below the thalamus, functioning as the main control center for the **autonomic nervous system** and the **endocrine system**.
 
• It produces the **Growth Hormone-Releasing Hormone (GHRH)**, frequently referred to as the **growth hormone-releasing factor**, which is a peptide hormone consisting of 44 amino acids.
 
• The hypothalamus releases **GHRH** into the **hypophyseal portal system**, a network of blood vessels that connects the hypothalamus to the **anterior pituitary gland**.
 
• Upon reaching the **anterior pituitary**, GHRH binds to specific receptors on **somatotropic cells**, triggering the synthesis and secretion of **Growth Hormone (GH)** or **somatotropin** into the bloodstream.
 
• The hypothalamus also produces **Somatostatin**, which acts as the **Growth Hormone-Inhibiting Hormone (GHIH)**, providing a regulatory feedback loop to maintain hormonal balance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pituitary Gland**:

 
 
• Often called the **Master Gland**, it is located in a bony cavity called the **sella turcica**.
 
• It is responsible for secreting the actual **Growth Hormone (GH)**, not the releasing factor.
 
 
 
• **Thyroid Gland**:
 
 
• Located in the neck region, it secretes **Thyroxine (T4)** and **Triiodothyronine (T3)**.
 
• These hormones regulate the **Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR)** and physical and mental growth.
 
 
 
• **Thymus Gland**:
 
 
• A lobular structure located between the lungs behind the **sternum**.
 
• It secretes **Thymosins**, which play a major role in the differentiation and maturation of **T-lymphocytes** for **cell-mediated immunity**.

questions.question: 'Laru Kaj' is a traditional festival celebrated by which community in Madhya Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gonds**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Laru Kaj** is a significant traditional and religious festival celebrated primarily by the **Gond tribe** in the **Mandla**, **Jabalpur**, and **Seoni** districts of **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• The festival is dedicated to **Lord Narayan Deo**, who is revered as the guardian deity of the household and the protector of the family.
 
• The central ritual of **Laru Kaj** involves the **sacrifice of a pig**, which is carried out with elaborate ceremonies to please the deity and seek blessings for **health, prosperity, and happiness**.
 
• This festival is not an annual event for every household; it is typically performed once every **nine or twelve years** by a family, or upon the fulfillment of a specific vow or during a marriage.
 
• During the celebration, traditional **Gondi songs** are sung, and community feasts are organized, reinforcing the social bonds and cultural heritage of the **Gond community**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhils**:

 
 
• Recognized as the largest tribal group in India, predominantly residing in **Dhar**, **Jhabua**, and **West Nimar**.
 
• They are famous for the **Bhagoria Haat** festival, a traditional celebration involving matchmaking and cultural dance.
 
 
 
• **Baigas**:
 
 
• Considered a **Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG)**, they reside mainly in the **Maikal range** of eastern Madhya Pradesh.
 
• They are known for their deep knowledge of **medicinal herbs** and traditional **Karma dance**.
 
 
 
• **Sahariyas**:
 
 
• Another **PVTG** concentrated in the northwestern districts like **Morena**, **Sheopur**, and **Gwalior**.
 
• They are traditionally **wood-cutters** and gatherers of forest produce, with a unique culture influenced by the **Rajasthan** border.

questions.question: Which of the following tiger reserve is notified as 56th tiger reserve of the country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Guru Ghasidas-Tamor Pingla tiger reserve**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change** officially notified the **Guru Ghasidas-Tamor Pingla Tiger Reserve** in **Chhattisgarh** as the **56th tiger reserve** of India in **November 2024**.
 
• This new reserve was formed by integrating the **Guru Ghasidas National Park** and the **Tamor Pingla Wildlife Sanctuary**, spanning across the districts of **Manendragarh-Chirmiri-Bharatpur**, **Koriya**, and **Surajpur**.
 
• It covers a massive area of approximately **2,829.38 square kilometers**, making it the **third largest tiger reserve** in the country, trailing only the **Nagarjunasagar Srisailam Tiger Reserve** in Andhra Pradesh and **Manas Tiger Reserve** in Assam.
 
• The notification follows the recommendation of the **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)**, aiming to strengthen the tiger habitat in the **Chota Nagpur plateau** and **Baghelkhand** regions.
 
• This reserve serves as a vital ecological corridor, connecting tiger populations between the **Sanjay-Dubri Tiger Reserve** in Madhya Pradesh and the **Palamau Tiger Reserve** in Jharkhand.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bandhavgarh Tiger Reserve**:

 
 
• Located in **Madhya Pradesh**, it is famous for having one of the highest densities of **Royal Bengal Tigers** in the world and houses the ancient **Bandhavgarh Fort**.
 
 
 
• **Sundarbans Tiger Reserve**:
 
 
• Situated in **West Bengal**, this **UNESCO World Heritage Site** is the largest **mangrove forest** globally and is the only mangrove habitat where tigers are found.
 
 
 
• **Kanha Tiger Reserve**:
 
 
• Located in **Madhya Pradesh**, it is the largest national park in Central India and is well-known for successfully reintroducing the **Barasingha** (Swamp Deer).
 
 
 
• **Tiger Conservation in India**:
 
 
• **Project Tiger** was launched on **April 1, 1973**, to protect the national animal. India currently hosts about **75 percent** of the global wild tiger population according to recent census data.

questions.question:
Which of the following organ of the human body is NOT imaged using ultrasounds?

I. Liver II. Gall bladder
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neither I nor II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ultrasound imaging**, also referred to as **sonography**, is a diagnostic medical procedure that uses high-frequency **sound waves** to produce visual representations of the inside of the body, particularly **soft tissues** and organs. ***Hence, statement I is incorrect.***
 
• The **Liver** is one of the primary organs evaluated through **abdominal ultrasound**. It allows clinicians to check for **hepatomegaly** (enlarged liver), **fatty liver disease**, **cirrhosis**, and **malignant tumors** or **cysts**. ***Hence, statement I is incorrect.***
 
• The **Gallbladder** is routinely and effectively imaged using ultrasound to detect **gallstones (cholelithiasis)**, inflammation known as **cholecystitis**, and blockages in the **bile ducts**. It is the gold standard for gallbladder evaluation due to its high sensitivity. ***Hence, statement II is incorrect.***
 
• Since both the **liver** and the **gallbladder** are standard organs that are frequently and successfully imaged using **ultrasound technology**, neither of them fits the criteria of an organ that is NOT imaged. ***Hence, statement II is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Diagnostic Scope of Ultrasound**:

 
 
• **Abdominal Imaging**: Beyond the liver and gallbladder, it is used for the **pancreas**, **spleen**, and **kidneys**.
 
• **Obstetrics**: Widely known for monitoring **fetal development** and **uterine health** during pregnancy.
 
• **Echocardiography**: A specialized ultrasound used to visualize **heart valves**, chambers, and blood flow patterns.
 
• **Limitations**: Ultrasound waves cannot easily penetrate **bone** or pass through **air/gas**. Consequently, organs like the **lungs** or the **gastrointestinal tract** (which contains gas) are difficult to image using this specific modality.
 
• **Safety**: Unlike **X-rays** or **CT scans**, ultrasound does not use **ionizing radiation**, making it safe for sensitive patients.

questions.question: In the context of Indian economy, which of the following is correct regarding Personal disposable Income (PDI)?

options.text: PDI = Personal Income - Personal tax payments + Non-tax payments
PDI = Personal Income - Personal tax payments - Non-tax payments
PDI = National Income - Personal tax payments + Non-tax payments
PDI = National Income - Personal tax payments - Non-tax payments

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**PDI = Personal Income - Personal tax payments - Non-tax payments**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Personal Disposable Income (PDI)** is the actual amount of income available to the **household sector** for **consumption** and **savings** after all mandatory government deductions are made.
 
• **Personal Income (PI)** refers to the total income received by individuals, including **wages**, **salaries**, **rent**, **interest**, and **transfer payments** (unearned income like pensions), before any direct taxes are subtracted.
 
• To calculate **PDI**, one must subtract **Personal Tax Payments**, which primarily consist of **direct taxes** such as **Income Tax**, **Wealth Tax**, and **Property Tax**.
 
• The calculation also requires the deduction of **Non-tax Payments**, which include miscellaneous payments to the government such as **fines**, **administrative fees**, **license fees**, and **penalties**.
 
• The fundamental equation used in **Macroeconomics** is: **PDI = Personal Income − Personal Tax Payments − Non-tax Payments**.
 
• This metric is a more accurate representation of the **purchasing power** of the public than **National Income** or **Personal Income** alone.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Income Flow in the Indian Economy**:

 
 
• **National Income (NI)** is the total value of goods and services produced. **Personal Income** is derived by subtracting **Undistributed Profits**, **Net Interest Payments** by households, and **Corporate Taxes** from **NI**, and adding **Transfer Payments**.
 
• **Disposable Income** is subsequently used to determine the **Average Propensity to Consume (APC)** and **Average Propensity to Save (APS)**.
 
 
 
• **Significance for Policy**:
 
 
• Changes in the **Income Tax slabs** in the **Union Budget** directly affect the **PDI** of the citizens.
 
• Higher **Personal Disposable Income** generally stimulates **aggregate demand** and encourages **economic growth** through increased **consumer spending**.

questions.question: When did the first Indian Open Golf Championship took place?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1964**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Open**, currently known as the **Hero Indian Open** due to sponsorship, was established in **1964** as the premier national open golf championship of India.
 
• The inaugural tournament was held at the prestigious **Delhi Golf Club (DGC)** in **New Delhi**, which has served as the most frequent venue in the history of the event.
 
• Legendary Australian golfer **Peter Thomson**, a five-time winner of **The Open Championship**, was the visionary behind the creation of this tournament to promote the sport in **Asia**.
 
• **Peter Thomson** cemented his legacy in Indian golf by winning the first-ever edition in **1964** with a total score of **292**.
 
• The championship is a vital stop on the **Asian Tour** and has been co-sanctioned by the **European Tour** (now the **DP World Tour**) since **2015**, attracting high-ranking international players.

• In **1965**, **Prem Gopal (P.G.) Sethi** made history by becoming the first amateur and the first Indian to win the **Indian Open** title.

questions.question: India and Bhutan have held the 6th Joint group of customs meeting in ____, from 24th-25th April 2025.
questions.solution:

__
 
• The **6th Joint Group of Customs (JGC)** meeting between **India** and **Bhutan** was scheduled to be held in **Thimphu**, the capital city of **Bhutan**, from **24th to 25th April 2025**.
 
• This high-level meeting serves as a critical institutional mechanism to discuss and resolve various issues related to **bilateral trade**, **transit**, and **customs cooperation** between the two neighboring nations.
 
• The primary objective of the **JGC** is to facilitate smoother movement of goods across the borders by streamlining **Customs procedures** and enhancing **connectivity** through **Land Customs Stations (LCS)**.
 
• The delegations typically involve senior officials from the **Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)** of India and the **Department of Revenue and Customs** of the Royal Government of Bhutan.
 
• Key agenda items often include the operationalization of **Integrated Check Posts (ICPs)**, the implementation of the **Electronic Cargo Tracking System (ECTS)**, and the notification of new **trade routes** to bolster economic ties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **India-Bhutan Trade Relations**:

 
 
• The bilateral trade relationship is governed by the **Agreement on Trade, Commerce, and Transit**, which provides for a **Free Trade** regime between the two countries.
 
• **India** remains **Bhutan's** largest trading partner, accounting for a significant majority of its total external trade.
 
• India provides **transit facilities** for Bhutanese trade with third countries through designated **entry and exit points** on the Indian border.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Cooperation**:
 
 
• The **Joint Group of Customs** meetings are essential for addressing **field-level bottlenecks** that traders face at **border crossings** such as **Jaigaon-Phuentsholing** and **Joghighopa**.
 
• Recent initiatives include the integration of **digital customs systems** to reduce the **turnaround time** for cargo and minimize physical documentation requirements.
 
• Collaborative efforts also focus on preventing the **smuggling** of controlled substances and wildlife products across the porous **Himalayan borders**.

questions.question: Who is the author of the book 'Indian Wisdom'?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Devdutt Pattanaik** is a prominent Indian mythologist, illustrator, and author widely recognized for his work on **sacred lore, folklore, and Hindu mythology**.
 
• He has authored the book **'Indian Wisdom'**, which distills complex philosophical ideas, rituals, and symbols from ancient Indian texts into simple, practical insights for contemporary life.
 
• His writing style uniquely integrates his own **hand-drawn illustrations** to explain deep-rooted cultural concepts from the Vedas, Upanishads, and epics like the **Mahabharata** and **Ramayana**.

• He is the founder of the **Isha Foundation**, a non-profit spiritual organization.
 
• His notable literary contributions include bestselling books like **'Inner Engineering: A Yogi's Guide to Joy'** and **'Karma: A Yogi's Guide to Crafting Your Destiny'**.
 
 
 
• **Deepak Chopra**:
 
 
• An Indian-American author and alternative medicine advocate who has written extensively on **mindfulness, spirituality, and holistic health**.
 
• His famous works include **'The Seven Spiritual Laws of Success'** and **'Ageless Body, Timeless Mind'**.
 
 
 
• **Radhakrishnan Pillai**:
 
 
• An academic and corporate trainer best known for researching and applying **Chanakya's ancient teachings** to modern management practices.

questions.question: In India, the RESET (Retired Sportsperson Empowerment Training) Programme was launched in _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2024**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **RESET Programme**, which stands for **Retired Sportsperson Empowerment Training**, was officially launched by the Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports, **Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya**, on **August 29, 2024**.
 
• The launch was strategically timed to coincide with **National Sports Day**, a day celebrated across India to honor the birth anniversary of the legendary hockey player **Major Dhyan Chand**.
 
• The primary aim of this initiative is to support athletes who have retired from active competition by providing them with the necessary **skills** and **training** to transition into new professional roles.
 
• The programme identifies that many athletes struggle after retirement; hence, it seeks to make them **employable** within the broader **sports ecosystem** or other corporate sectors by bridging the gap between their athletic achievements and career requirements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eligibility and Scope**:

 
 
• The programme is designed for retired sportspersons in the age bracket of **20 to 50 years**.
 
• Candidates must have represented **India** at the **international level** or secured medals in recognized national competitions like the **National Games** or **Khelo India Games**.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Alignment**:
 
 
• The initiative is aligned with the goals of the **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020**, which emphasizes **vocational training** and lifelong learning opportunities.
 
• By empowering these individuals, the government aims to utilize their expertise as **mentors**, **coaches**, or **sports administrators**, thereby strengthening India's grassroots sports structure.
 
 
 
• **Career Support**:
 
 
• Participants receive training in modern sports technologies, **management**, and leadership, ensuring they remain relevant in the evolving job market.
 
• It helps address the **socio-economic security** of athletes who have dedicated their youth to representing the nation.
